ei.title: 억양을 사회적 정체성의 표식으로 신뢰할 수 있는 이유

fullPassage: Language can be used to lie, but it can also be a reliable signal. Quite independent of what you say, the accent you say it with reveals things about who you are — where you grew up, your socioeconomic status, which side of the tracks you are from. Your accent is a tag, telling people which social category you’re in. Not unlike the stories we tell and the greetings we give, this kind of tag defines your social relationship with others. It says who you are more likely to be affiliated with. And unlike the choice of how to pronounce the word Hi when you greet someone at the door, your accent is less under your flexible control. It is harder to fake.

questions.passage: Language can be used to lie, but it can also be a (A)[unreliable / reliable] signal. Quite independent of what you say, the accent you say it with reveals things about who you are — where you grew up, your socioeconomic status, which side of the tracks you are from. Your accent is a tag, telling people which social category you’re in. Not unlike the stories we tell and the greetings we give, this kind of tag (B)[defines / confuses] your social relationship with others. It says who you are more likely to be affiliated with. And unlike the choice of how to pronounce the word Hi when you greet someone at the door, your accent is less under your flexible control. It is harder to (C)[fake / prove].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 신뢰할 수 있는(reliable), 정의하다(defines), 위조하다(fake)가 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reliable — defines — fake: 언어는 '신뢰할 수 있는' 신호이고, 꼬리표가 관계를 '정의'하며, 억양은 '위조'하기 어려움.
❌ ② unreliable — defines — fake: (A) 첫 문장에서 신뢰할 수 있다고 함.
❌ ③ reliable — confuses — fake: (B) 관계를 '혼란시키는' 것이 아니라 '정의'함.
❌ ④ reliable — defines — prove: (C) '증명'이 아니라 '위조'하기 어려움.
det.tip: reliable(신뢰할 수 있는) ↔ unreliable(신뢰할 수 없는)

questions.passage: Language can be used to lie, but it can also be a reliable signal. Quite independent of what you say, the accent you say it with (A)[reveals / hides] things about who you are — where you grew up, your socioeconomic status, which side of the tracks you are from. Your accent is a (B)[mystery / tag], telling people which social category you’re in. Not unlike the stories we tell and the greetings we give, this kind of tag defines your social relationship with others. It says who you are more likely to be affiliated with. And unlike the choice of how to pronounce the word Hi when you greet someone at the door, your accent is less under your (C)[flexible / strict] control. It is harder to fake.

det.korean: 드러내다(reveals), 꼬리표(tag), 유연한(flexible)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ reveals — tag — flexible: 억양이 정보를 '드러내고', '꼬리표' 역할을 하며, '유연한' 통제 하에 있음.
❌ ① hides — tag — flexible: (A) 억양은 정보를 '숨기는' 것이 아니라 '드러냄'.
❌ ② reveals — mystery — flexible: (B) 억양은 '수수께끼'가 아니라 '꼬리표'.
❌ ④ reveals — tag — strict: (C) '엄격한' 통제가 아니라 '유연한' 통제.

questions.passage: Language can be used to lie, but it can also be a reliable signal. (A)[Barely / Quite] independent of what you say, the accent you say it with reveals things about who you are — where you grew up, your socioeconomic status, which side of the tracks you are from. Your accent is a tag, telling people which (B)[social / personal] category you’re in. Not unlike the stories we tell and the greetings we give, this kind of tag defines your social relationship with others. It says who you are more likely to be (C)[affiliated / competing] with. And unlike the choice of how to pronounce the word Hi when you greet someone at the door, your accent is less under your flexible control. It is harder to fake.

det.korean: 상당히(Quite), 사회적(social), 제휴된(affiliated)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Quite — social — affiliated: 말하는 내용과 '상당히' 무관하게 억양이 '사회적' 범주와 '제휴' 관계를 드러냄.
❌ ① Quite — social — competing: (C) '경쟁하는'이 아니라 '제휴된'.
❌ ③ Barely — social — affiliated: (A) '거의 ~않게'는 문맥과 반대. 억양은 말 내용과 무관하게 드러냄.
❌ ④ Quite — personal — affiliated: (B) '개인적' 범주가 아니라 '사회적' 범주.
det.tip: Quite independent of = ~와 상당히 무관하게, affiliated with = ~와 제휴된
